findings.reason: the deliverable's whole claim is "answered from the last computed result", and without a landed-marker assertion the suite cannot tell a working refresh from one that never stores.
findings.text: the done-when asserts only that the route serves the prior result with an age header while the recompute runs; it never asserts that the recompute's result then becomes the served one, so a child that computes but writes nothing (or to the wrong key) passes every discovery, rollup and checks case

findings.reason: a control that cannot exceed the bound proves nothing, so the plan must name a fixture (or a deliberate delay) heavy enough that the inline path exceeds 50 ms, or the case rests on a control that never fires.
findings.text: the four cases run "for a temporary project" and each negative control "computes that route inline", then asserts "the trivial-request bound then fails"; but discovery, rollup and checks over one temporary project compute in single-digit milliseconds, well under the 50 ms bound, so the inline control need not make the bound fail and is not shown to fire

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_start_check_refresh`/`_spawn_check_refresh` (reckon/serve.py:3151,3147), `_CHECK_REFRESHES` (:1474), `_FleetChangeWatch` (:351), `_send_project_changes` (:3542), `_serve_velocity` (:3631), `collect_projects` (:1313), `compliance.project_checks` (reckon/compliance.py:247), `watchProjectStateChanges` (docs/ui/state-loader.js:697), `VelocityView` (docs/ui/velocity.jsx:183), `tests/test_spa_crew_cards.py`, and §8's 605.8 s anchor all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: two findings — the measure shows the stale-serve path but never that a recomputed result becomes the served one, and the inline negative control is not shown to exceed the bound it must fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs and the srv-1006 latency watch sit under the run directory per §2's shared terms and §9's lands; nothing is written to a scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach the new symbols; the §-references are the plan's own section ids in prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the cited costs match §1's evidence (checks 2.2–2.7 s, velocity 10.5 s), the child-process-plus-stored-result mechanism is capable of the under-50 ms answer the done-when asserts, and each of the four routes names the production caller that spawns its refresh (`_send_project_changes`, the `/_checks` pending-document spawn, `_FleetChangeWatch`, `_serve_velocity`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one goal: answer a request from the last computed result rather than behind a recompute, applied to the four routes with the client that consumes them.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5's declared depends-on [s3, s8] matches its text ("Build it after §3 and §8 merge"), §8 is done, and the §16 it relies on for `reckon/change_streams.py` orders before it transitively through §3 (whose depends-on carries s16).
